findings.prior_scope: The hwilum-source sense is productive from ch09 only as sometimes; its scope expressly excludes the separate a while gloss. The prior form analysis literally describes an adverb of frequency.
findings.resolution: Retain the supported model phrase. Preserve the old frequency form/sense and add a distinct supplied contextual form, hwilum-u18-earlier-source, with a distinct supplied earlier-time sense and visible whole-phrase support.
findings.help: Hwīlum ǣr — a while ago; formerly, on the earlier visit. This is not the frequency meaning sometimes.
findings.morphology_status: Same attested surface; distinct supplied contextual identity avoids rewriting the prior frequency analysis.
findings.sense_status: supplied earlier-time sense; no independent production promotion

findings.prior_scope: Gefyl morphology is productive from ch06; the fill sense and accusative container are productive from ch08. The explicit ch17 contents frame names afyllan, not gefyllan. A general means label does not itself bind the current material complement.
findings.resolution: Retain gefyl and supply the complete command/container/contents frame. BT Supplement330a directly supports the prefixed verb's material construction.
findings.help: Gefyl hiera saccas mid hwǣte — Fill their sacks with wheat. Gefyl is a command to one steward; hiera saccas is the accusative plural container, and mid hwǣte names its contents, with dative singular hwǣte.
findings.morphology_status: Existing imperative and nominal forms retained.
findings.sense_status: Existing gefyllan fill sense retained; material-complement interpretation is locally supplied.
findings.construction_status: supplied complete gefyllan plus accusative container plus mid-dative contents frame
findings.source_distinction: Crawford193 Genesis44.1 actually prints Fille, with fylle/fyl apparatus variants. It corroborates sacks plus mid hwæte, but does not directly attest gefyl; prefixed lexical evidence is independent.

findings.prior_scope: Morgen morphology and morning sense are productive from ch01. Earlier temporal on teaching expressly covers a numbered day; current bare On help does not state the complete phrase's case.
findings.resolution: Retain the attested endingless phrase and the existing accusative singular morgen identity; supply its complete temporal meaning and case locally.
findings.help: On morgen — in the morning; morgen is accusative singular in this temporal expression. Learn the complete expression here.
findings.morphology_status: Existing morgen-acc-sg retained; no new dative form inferred.
findings.sense_status: Existing morning sense retained; temporal preposition is supplied.
findings.construction_status: supplied complete temporal expression; no general on government promotion
findings.source_distinction: Crawford main text has On mergen; the L apparatus has morgen. BT directly prints On morgen.

findings.prior_scope: Prior leof-1 means dear. Unit11's standalone address construction explicitly teaches weak superlatives leofosta/leofoste, not this positive sir address.
findings.resolution: Retain the exact prior nominative masculine singular strong-adjective form analysis and surface. Add a distinct supplied substantival/address sense and contextual use note; assign no new productive nominal system.
findings.help: Lēof — Sir, a respectful address to the steward. It stands alone here and is not an adjective modifying a following noun.
findings.sense_status: new supplied address sense; prior dear sense unchanged

findings.prior_scope: The existing supplied aetforan-source record explicitly specifies dative him. The separately taught beforan accusative positioning construction does not license an extension to aetforan.
findings.resolution: Correct the unsupported accusative extension to dative him. BTMain21b and Wright295§559(3) explicitly give dative aetforan; Wright's list allowing additional accusative names beforan, not aetforan. Preserve the old model and binding as a superseded witness.
help: Ætforan ūs — before us, in our presence; ūs is dative.
Cuman ætforan him — come before him, into his presence; him is dative after ætforan. A verb of motion does not automatically require an accusative after every preposition.
findings.morphology_status: Reuse actual prior he-m-dat-sg; do not relabel the old accusative identity.
findings.sense_status: Existing supplied aetforan sense retained with explicit government.

model_change.new_context: dative masculine singular complement of aetforan

findings.alternative_judgment: The independent dative answer is supported valid language, not a failure to reproduce the unsupported accusative model.
findings.bounded_negative_finding: No positive accusative evidence was found in the checked sources; no claim about every possible historical occurrence is made.

separate_47_06_confirmation.finding: Retain the model. Earlier dative-location teaching and Crawford194 Genesis44.14 support the place of prostration. Actual selected preposition is beforan, not aetforan. No additional productive assignment is required.
